### [Anthropic update on independent evaluators](https://www.anthropic.com/news/an-update-on-independent-evaluators)

**Anthropic** · 2026-10-15

Anthropic has granted employee-like access to non-profit evaluator METR and partnered with SecureBio and Accenture to conduct third-party AI safety and risk assessments.

- METR received deep, employee-like system access to conduct risk assessments and will publicly publish its findings.
- Anthropic is expanding its third-party evaluation network by collaborating with SecureBio and Accenture, and initiating early discussions with Hugging Face.
- The evaluation model uses an approach similar to banking supervision, placing resident external examiners inside the company to evaluate risks that cannot be publicly disclosed due to security or commercial sensitivity.

**Why it matters:** Granting external evaluators deep internal access helps establish independent safety oversight without publicly leaking sensitive compute, training, or potentially dangerous technical information.

### [Offering expanded Claude access across all three branches of government](https://www.anthropic.com/news/offering-expanded-claude-access-across-all-three-branches-of-government)

**Anthropic** · 2026-10-15

Anthropic is offering one-year access to Claude for Enterprise and Claude for Government to all three U.S. federal branches for $1.

- Package includes both Claude for Enterprise and Claude for Government with access to Anthropic's frontier models and technical support for one year.
- Claude for Government models are certified for FedRAMP High workloads to handle sensitive unclassified government data.
- Deployment expands on GSA schedule integration and existing enterprise infrastructure partnerships with AWS, Google Cloud, and Palantir.
- Existing government usage includes a Department of Defense agreement with a $200 million ceiling, daily deployment for 10,000 researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, and multi-language support for the DC Department of Health.

**Why it matters:** By removing cost barriers, federal agencies across all three branches can deploy FedRAMP High-certified AI models on existing infrastructure for sensitive work.

### [Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/15/anthropic-tells-investors/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-10-15

Anthropic reported Q3 revenue of $16.8bn to investors, up nearly 50% from Q2, while clamping down on rival AI labs distilling its models.

- Quarterly revenue grew from ~$4.8bn in Q1 to $11.5bn in Q2, reaching $16.8bn in Q3.
- Q3 unit economics showed $1.70 in revenue generated for every $1 spent on computing power, with adjusted operating margins at 11%.
- Model distillation by competitor labs previously accounted for 5% to 7% of revenue before Anthropic materially restricted the practice in Q3.
- Calculations indicate competitor labs spent over $500m distilling Anthropic's models in Q2 alone.

**Why it matters:** Anthropic's reported revenue surge and positive compute margins demonstrate commercial scaling, while its crackdown on model distillation cuts off rivals from leveraging its model outputs.
